💡 Ideas

Two brothers are driving to town at night, maybe to the cinema or a party. The story is called "A Strange Accident" — so something happened to the car… but what? Read on!

Reading

Read the story. Then put the pictures in the correct order.

📖 How to read: read the story quickly first. Do not stop at every word. Then look at the pictures A–I and number them 1–9 in the order of the story.

LAST MONTH, two brothers, sixteen-year-old George and eighteen-year-old David, were on their own at home one Saturday afternoon. Their parents were on a weekend trip with some friends. They were in their dad's car. George was bored and wanted to have an adventure.

"Let's drive into town this evening," he suggested to David. "You're 18. You can drive Mum's car."

David wasn't happy about it because he wasn't allowed to drive his mum's car. But he was bored too, so he agreed.

The boys arrived in the town centre, and decided to go to the cinema. David parked the car carefully outside the cinema. They watched a great film. They were hungry after the film, so they stopped at a café and ordered a pizza.

Their friends, Sally and Emily, were there. "We're going to a nightclub now," said Sally. "Do you want to come?" The boys weren't tired, so they agreed. When they arrived at the nightclub, David parked the car carefully in the street.

George and David stayed in the nightclub for a long time. When they walked back to the car, they noticed something terrible.

"Oh, no!" shouted David. "There's a big dent in the back of the car!"

The boys were very worried. They hurried home, and waited until 7 a.m. Then they phoned a garage and explained the problem. A mechanic repaired the car, and the boys parked it outside the house just in time!

A few minutes later, their parents returned home. The boys were too scared to say anything about the car. But later that day, their mother wanted to use her car. "Hey! Come and look at this!" she shouted. The boys were very nervous. "I think Mum is angry," said George. But she wasn't angry. She looked very surprised. She continued, "I don't understand! A van crashed into my car last Thursday, but now you can't even see the dent!" 🟠

Reading · details

True or False?

Read the story again. Are the sentences true or false? If it is false, find the mistake!

1. George and David were alone at home.

2. George and David's parents were on a day trip with their friends.

3. Both boys were bored at home.

4. George and David's friends, Sally and Emily, were at the cinema.

5. David believed that he caused the dent.

6. The mechanic repaired the dent before their parents arrived home.

7. The dent was there before George and David used the car.

Grammar

Past Simple vs Past Continuous

📌 Remember: use Past Continuous (was/were + -ing) for a longer action or the background of the story. Use Past Simple for actions and events one after another.

✔ They were walking back to the car when they noticed a dent. (long action + short event)
✔ They watched a film and then ordered a pizza. (events one after another)

Choose the correct form.

1. While they ___ back to the car, they noticed a dent.

2. They ___ a great film and then went to a café.

3. What ___ when the storm started?

4. The wind ___ their tent away while they were in the forest.

5. ___ your parents angry when you came home late?

6. We ___ pizza when Sally and Emily arrived.

7. Dad ___ the car and turned the key.

8. At 7 a.m. the boys ___ a garage.

Speaking / Writing

Retell the story

Retell "A Strange Accident" in your own words. Use the prompts below — click them to highlight. Start every sentence with a different prompt.

Last month…One Saturday afternoon… George wanted…, so he…First, they… / Then, they… While they were…, they noticed…They were worried, so… When their parents came home…In the end, …
🎤 Model answer

Last month, two brothers, George and David, were home alone because their parents were on a weekend trip. George was bored, so he suggested driving into town in Mum's car. First, they went to the cinema, and then they ordered a pizza at a café. Their friends Sally and Emily invited them to a nightclub, and they agreed. While they were walking back to the car, they noticed a big dent in the back of it! They were very worried, so they hurried home and phoned a garage at 7 a.m. A mechanic repaired the car just in time. When their parents came home, their mother was surprised, not angry: a van had crashed into the car the Thursday before, and now the dent was gone!

Listening · The Storm in the Forest

Listen to another story

A family goes camping in a forest. Something goes very wrong! Listen and do the tasks.

📄 Audio script (open after listening!)

Last Friday night, the Carter family — Dad, Mum and sixteen-year-old Ben — drove to Blackwood Forest for a weekend of camping. Ben wasn't excited about "family time", but he had a plan: he was filming everything for his video blog.

On Saturday morning they put up their tent by the lake, and then hiked to an old abandoned watchtower in the hills. Ben was climbing the tower steps when the sky suddenly went black. "We need to go. Now," said Dad.

They were running back along the path when lightning hit a pine tree right in front of them. The tree crashed down and blocked the trail, so they had to fight their way through the bushes. When they finally reached the campsite, the scene was a disaster: the wind had torn their tent out of the ground, and their things were scattered everywhere — Mum's bag was in a tree, and Dad's boots were floating in the lake.

Dad jumped into the car and turned the key. Nothing. He tried again and again — the engine was completely dead. No signal on the phones. Rain was pouring down, and it was getting dark.

Then Ben noticed something strange: a small light, moving between the trees. "Did you see that?" he whispered. They had no choice — they walked towards it.

The light came from a wooden cabin. Inside, a group of hikers was already sheltering from the storm, together with an old forest ranger and his enormous dog. The ranger looked at Dad and laughed: "Engine dead? Third car this week. The lake water gets into everything." He gave them hot tea, and when the rain stopped, two hikers helped him fix the car with some old jumper cables.

They drove home at sunrise, soaked, exhausted and starving. Dad looked in the mirror and said, "Adventure holiday. Ten out of ten. Never again."

Two days later, Ben uploaded his video — "Our Camping Trip Went VERY Wrong" — and it got over 50,000 views. Mum said the storm was a nightmare. Ben said it was the best weekend of his life.

📚 New words from the story

WordMeaning
put up a tentto build a tent
campsitea place where people camp
weather forecasta prediction of what the weather will be
stormvery bad weather with rain, strong wind and thunder
lightninga bright flash of electricity in the sky
blow away (blew away)to carry something away with the wind
scatterto spread things over a large area, in many directions
the engine wouldn't startthe car engine did not work
wave at / flag downto make a signal to a driver to stop
rangera person whose job is to look after a forest or park
repair servicepeople you call to fix something broken, e.g. a car
check the forecastto look at the weather prediction before a trip
